reviews.title: From Hero to ZERO!
reviews.text:
Updated 31 October 2026:

I have previously given the app five stars. It was a great app for a long time. Some of us purchased the premium version of the app. We were told that it was a lifetime deal. Well, I am still alive and they reneged on that deal. They now expect us to pay every month. That’s just plain bad business. 

As a software developer myself, I had also sold software for a one-time price with free updates and technical support for life. I eventually had to stop offering that deal, but I never even considered for a second screwing over the very people who helped me build my business by giving me their business!

Their greed will catch up with them!

reviews.title: When it comes to AI editing, it creates far more work than it completes.
reviews.text: I wrote a detailed review of Bazaart that, for reasons unknown, was never publicly displayed in the App Store and is now gone. I paid $24.99 for one month (which ended today) and 1,000 AI credits, roughly 90% of which were wasted on failed renders, distorted images, and unusable results. Their AI consistently created more work than it saved, requiring repeated attempts and extensive manual corrections. Bazaart refused to refund what I understood to be a refundable free trial, despite the product's poor performance. The company then responded to my missing review with, “Please reach out to us again through the Help Center in the app, and we'll take a closer look.” I did exactly that and was ignored - 2 weeks and counting.

reviews.title: So disappointed!
reviews.text: I was one of Bazaart’s early users and even upgraded to the lifetime Premium plan because I genuinely believed in the app and wanted to support its development. What made Bazaart special was the freedom it gave users to create from scratch without feeling restricted. Over the years, it allowed me to explore my creativity in ways other editing apps simply didn’t. That’s why the recent subscription changes are so disappointing. I now find myself locked out of basic features, including certain eraser options, unless I pay for another subscription. I understand that developing and integrating new AI tools costs money, and I have no issue with advanced AI features being part of a separate paid plan. But basic editing tools that have existed for years and have nothing to do with AI should not suddenly be placed behind another paywall, especially for customers who purchased lifetime Premium. As a long-term supporter, it feels as though the value of my lifetime purchase has been reduced after the fact. I have years of work and experience invested in Bazaart, so being asked to pay monthly to continue using features I previously had access to is incredibly frustrating. I supported Bazaart because it once felt different from other companies. Unfortunately, this decision makes loyal users feel penalised rather than valued. Unless this changes, I’ll reluctantly be looking for an alternative.

reviews.title: DYB designs
reviews.text: I previously gave this app 5 stars. However, with all of the changes, I was considered for years a lifetime Premium member, your APP had erased my status. Not everyone uses or requires AI use. Now payments have been added to premium users for years due to AI features that I NEVER used and have no need to use it and they have erased all of my work that was supposed to be in the cloud and visibly seen in my account/projects but they are gone. I wrote to customer care but not a reply & the issue isn’t fixed. It doesn’t matter because now you can only have cloud activity if a paying member for a ridiculous amount of money per year. If corrected I’d gladly change my review. But it’s difficult to give 5 stars when I have been a loyal user, to the point I deleted all other apps like this one. But trust I have uploaded them again to use. “Lifetime” doesn’t mean lifetime to Bazaart because as of August 2026 a payment is necessary to keep using the app in Premium status. Very disappointed to say the least.

reviews.title: Removing features I paid for
reviews.text:
I bought Bazaart all the way back in 2016 and I’ve used it on and off pretty heavily since. I generally like the app. It’s great for editing photos, or how I usually use it, making memes. The main problem I’ve run into recently is that they’ve started putting features that I’ve always had access to behind another pay wall. Which is silly, didn’t I already buy your app? I don’t want to use your AI nonsense. All I want is fonts and the ability to edit my photos easily. Stop pushing your premium on me, and stop pushing AI. I enjoyed the app but if you keep taking features away I will go somewhere else. 

Also, on a separate note but for the love of god, can we please call fonts by their actual name instead of whatever ridiculous system y’all have come up with? It’s impossible to find anything I’m looking for. Let me search by font name. I just want to use comic sans!!

reviews.title: Not good for image editing
reviews.text: Easy to use, nice layout/blueprint, and the ready-made prompts are helpful. But I didn’t use the image generation from scratch, I just wanted specific details changed on images I’d already taken. For that purpose, the AI on this app isn’t very mature, unable to carry out a prompt correctly or even at all, either completely ignoring an instruction, or following the instruction but with a poor outcome. The image quality is also really low so an image looks worse quality after it’s been edited than the original. Decent enough if it was £2.99 a month, but not worth £12.99 at all. Unsubscribed and deleted.

reviews.title: Another Disappointed Long Time User
reviews.text: This is my first time ever writing an app review just because of how disappointed I am. I’ve had this app since like 2014. To see what it’s like today is so sad compared to the day I downloaded it. The most basic functions are now hidden behind a paywall and the AI functions are the forefront. I also saw how other people were complaining about paying for “Premium Forever” but you said it actually ends August 1st of this year, that doesn’t sound like “Forever” to me. Even if it said it in the fine print that it actually ends on a certain date - I think that’s not only a bad business practice but shady. I have no interest in paying you $80+ a year to use a basic tool like “remove” and my OWN fonts if there’s a possibility you just swoop in before a year ends and tell me that my premium status is over early. I understand you wanting/needing to make a profit off of this app but this is way too much. I’m unfortunately going to look for a new editing app because I doubt you’ll listen to our pleads.

reviews.title: Consistently Disappointing
reviews.text: I've had this app since 2019 and really enjoyed the features they offered. My first issue arose back in 2020 when I got a new phone and learned that my projects were saved locally on a device and would not be backed up even if my phone was. Fast forward a couple of years and they start charging for features that used to be free, add a watermark that can only be removed by paying a fee (which they eventually removed), and most recently force AI integration in the app. Bazaart has become less of a tool for artists and just another machine to produce AI slop. Now my second and biggest issue of all came last week, when all of my projects disappeared for a SECOND time. I didn't delete app nor did I update my phone this time however this conveniently occurred at the same time they began promoting their premium account access that will save your projects to a cloud.. for another fee. Another great app lost to the parasite of capitalism.

reviews.title: RIP Baazart
reviews.text:
Bazaart used to be one of my favorite creative apps, but the recent obsession with AI has completely changed what made it great. Before AI was pushed into everything, the app felt focused, reliable, and designed for people who actually wanted to create. Now it feels like Bazaart is just copying every other creator app on the market instead of building on what originally made it unique.

The AI features don’t work as well as the tools they replaced, and the overall experience feels less polished than it did before. It’s disappointing to see a company that once empowered creativity jump on the same trend as everyone else.

What’s even more frustrating is that the creative industry is already facing uncertainty, and many companies seem more interested in replacing human creativity with AI than supporting the artists, designers, and creators who helped build these platforms in the first place.

Bazaart had its own identity. Now it feels like just another AI app trying to follow the crowd. A real shame.

reviews.title: Loved it at first, then too glitchy for iPad use
reviews.text:
Jan 2026 UPDATE: I discontinued my subscription after the latest big update last month. Very little works on my iPad as it should, and the app crashes *constantly*. I tried to create a simple static graphic using an image from my camera roll and two text boxes, and the Bazaart app crashed SIX TIMES. The devs seem so focused on the new development that they can’t keep basic functionality running anymore. My team and I have switched to Canva. Very disappointing.

UPDATED: The developers fixed some of the glitches as of December, 2024.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: This app made my life so much easier when I first started using it a year ago, but recent updates have made previously-working functions break. The first thing I noticed was the outline feature stopped working on text. Then it stopped working on photos. Then shapes. I submitted tickets and screen captures of the steps I took, and they stated it had been resolved, but it has not been fixed. Recently other features have stopped working as well. And, the app has been crashing at least once per week since July-ish. I have been using it on a 2024 iPad Pro 11”. I’m going to have to move back to Canva, which I previously had stopped using in favor of Bazaart. I love this app so much, I would happily pay more for premium membership, but I am not going to pay for something that routinely forces me to have to find work arounds. Bummer.
